observed objects and assessment: Greek-style crested bronze helmet, short chiton, leather torso harness, strapped sandals; self/recurved bow, arrow and quiver. Both string segments and arrow nock visible; right draw and left bow grips coherent.
fault and fix: Leather crossover cuirass and calf-high sandal straps feel costume-like; wide aiming pose differs from calm standing set. Repaint standing archer in simple chiton, low footwear and restrained helmet.

observed objects and assessment: Late-sixteenth-century morion, slashed doublet/hose, powder charges, closed shoes; gun on forked rest. Both hands support stock.
fault and fix: Thick glowing match rises away from pan while muzzle fires; lock reads invented. Repaint standing with an identifiable matchlock at rest and a thin slow match held by the serpentine, no firing smoke.

observed objects and assessment: Twentieth-century split-trail field gun: long bore, recoil cylinder, shield, rubber tyres and grounded trails. No human anatomy.
fault and fix: Retain; mechanically coherent at available source detail.

observed objects and assessment: Speculative tracked unmanned armoured vehicle, turret gun, sensor heads, smoke launchers and connected tracks. No historical exact-model claim.
fault and fix: Retain; distinct sensor silhouette and neutral disc.

observed objects and assessment: Self bow and fletched arrow, quiver, fur hood, hide/wool clothes, leather boots; right hand at nock and left around grip.
fault and fix: Upper string disappears before reaching bow tip; lower segment also incomplete. Edit both continuous tip-to-nock segments; retain figure if possible. Wide firing stance is a secondary poor set match.

observed objects and assessment: Medieval steel-prod crossbow, tiller and foot stirrup; hood, padded layers, bolts, leather boots; hands pull cord.
fault and fix: Foot rests on flexible prod beside empty stirrup, not in stirrup; spanning cord geometry is confused. Repaint standing at rest with intact crossbow, supported stock and visible string.

observed objects and assessment: Seventeenth-century buff coat, slouch hat, powder bandolier, matchlock and boots. Right hand at trigger and left under stock; match cord and pan visible.
fault and fix: Kneeling firing tableau, smoke and very ragged patchwork dominate; smaller body scale. Repaint standing with weapon at rest; simplify costume.

observed objects and assessment: Kettle hat, padded gambeson, boots and two-handed polearm.
fault and fix: Weapon is a short hooked axe/bill, not the pike named by the unit; raised striking pose compounds mismatch. Repaint standing brigand with long straight pike, both hands on shaft.

observed objects and assessment: Horn suspended by cord, belt axe, fur mantle and wrapped boots; one hand shades eyes, other rests on thigh; fingers plausible.
fault and fix: Kneeling figure is squat against standing set; fantasy-heavy fur and massive leather cuffs. Repaint upright scout with restrained Iron Age wool and leather.

observed objects and assessment: Iron Age spear with socketed head, hide-faced oval bossed shield, short sword and leather boots. Spear is complete.
fault and fix: Left fingers curl around near rim rather than centre grip behind boss; shield support is mechanically wrong. Edit shield and left forearm to a centre grip; standing stance preferred.

observed objects and assessment: WWI-style radial-engine biplane with two wings, struts, wooden two-blade propeller, tailplane, open cockpit and landing wheels.
fault and fix: Wheel hubs float inside empty rims; spokes/discs were lost or never painted. Edit to fabric-covered wheel discs; preserve aircraft and display stand.

observed objects and assessment: WWII twin-engine medium bomber, two three-blade props, glazed cockpit/nose, dorsal turret, twin tail fins; coherent wings and stand.
fault and fix: Retain; no clear broken connection or wrong-period component seen.

observed objects and assessment: Circlet, scale armour, embroidered purple mantle, labarum-like staff with Christian devices, boots; right fist grips staff and left gathers cloth.
fault and fix: Raised second step on base differs from plain disc. Double-headed eagle is a later dynastic cue whose intended date needs clarification; do not certify it for AD 1000. Simplify base when revisited.

observed objects and assessment: Classical armoured horseman: scale barding, masked helmet, two-handed kontos and boots. Both grips connect to lance.
fault and fix: Visible stirrup is anachronistic for Classical Greco-Roman cavalry; horse is extremely short-legged and lance short for a kontos. Remove stirrups and lengthen horse proportions in a repaint.

observed objects and assessment: Nineteenth-century cavalryman: kepi, wool uniform, gauntlets, sabre with knucklebow, saddle/bridle/reins, boots and stirrup; four horse limbs distinguishable.
fault and fix: Charging horse and raised sabre are action tableau; shorten excess base width and use standing horse on next repaint. Kit otherwise plausible.

observed objects and assessment: Scythian/Persian-inspired cap, patterned tunic/trousers, boots, decorated quiver; horn-and-wood recurved bow has continuous string to nock, coherent draw grip.
fault and fix: Kneeling pose, oversized head and ornamental costume differ from standing adult set. Repaint upright; preserve recognisable recurved bow.

observed objects and assessment: Medieval kettle hat, gambeson, boots, rectangular pavise and steel crossbow.
fault and fix: Stock/prod appears to pass through the unbroken pavise; no notch or clearance. Repaint standing with crossbow held wholly beside a grounded pavise, clear hands and string.

observed objects and assessment: Late-sixteenth/early-seventeenth-century three-quarter plate, close helmet, wheellock pistol, sheathed sword, boots/stirrups and reins. Pistol wheel stylised but recognisable.
fault and fix: Horse has compressed pony-like proportions; firing smoke and outstretched pistol pose. Repaint standing cavalryman on proportionate horse, pistol at rest.

observed objects and assessment: Three speculative two-rotor camera drones above neutral disc; original source only 256 px, so tiny mechanical detail cannot be authenticated.
fault and fix: Low-resolution source softens panel view; no visible support is an intentional flying-subject convention. Replace with higher-resolution own painting later.

observed objects and assessment: Mexica macuahuitl with dark inserted blades, round chimalli, eagle head suit, feathered textile and sandals. Hand wraps weapon handle; shield arm occluded.
fault and fix: Large loose overlapping feather suit and wing-like sleeves read costume rather than fitted tlahuiztli; striking pose. Repaint standing with restrained fitted eagle suit; do not invent visible hidden grip.

observed objects and assessment: Industrial/Napoleonic artilleryman with shako, uniform, gaiters, sponge staff and bronze muzzle-loader on wood/spoked carriage. Both hands visible, one on staff and one on breech.
fault and fix: Retain. Current data calls this Industrial, so shako is not a Renaissance anachronism despite old README wording.

observed objects and assessment: WWII single-engine fighter, four-blade propeller, exhaust stubs, enclosed cockpit, tapered wings and tailplane on curved stand.
fault and fix: Painting coherent; separate small-icon concern carried from prior audit.

observed objects and assessment: Celtic warrior with torc, leaf-head spear, bossed oval shield, trousers and boots; spear and grip continuous, shield hand hidden.
fault and fix: Action pose and decorative blue spirals are poorly evidenced. Polybius describes Gaesatae fighting naked at Telamon after removing clothes; this clothed figure can represent one at rest, but not that specific battle. Repaint a historically grounded standing figure; do not call trousers universally impossible.

observed objects and assessment: Ancient Greek rider with crested helmet, spear, round shield on back, chiton, sandals, reins and saddlecloth.
fault and fix: Visible support under sandal reads as a stirrup, anachronistic for Greek cavalry; bronze forearm cuffs are unsupported costume. Edit to freely hanging sandalled feet and bare forearms.

observed objects and assessment: Early-twentieth-century short heavy barrel, shield, recoil cradle, steel-rimmed spoked wheels, elevating gear and trail.
fault and fix: Trail foot floats outside disc rather than bearing on ground. Extend plain base enough to support it; current gun remains legible.

observed objects and assessment: Speculative four-legged robot with sensors and belt-fed gun; four feet/legs discernible, feed box and rounds visible.
fault and fix: Tiny transparent square holes at joint flanges and near upper-left head edge look keyed away; the main joints are connected, not severed. Restore opaque metal locally; cold grey base should match cream set.

observed objects and assessment: WWII US-style M1 helmet, field jacket, web kit, canvas leggings, boots, grenade and upright wooden rifle; fingers visible on grenade and fore-end.
fault and fix: Raised straight-arm grenade pose looks like presenting it; rifle receiver/trigger area indistinct and not securely identifiable as Garand. Repaint standing with correctly formed rifle at rest.

observed objects and assessment: Cold-War eight-engine bomber, four twin pods, swept wings, tall fin, glazed nose, curved display stand.
fault and fix: Retain; all eight intakes and four pod attachments visible. Generic rather than exact B-52 replica.

observed objects and assessment: Early swept-wing jet with nose intake, wings, tailplane and display stand.
fault and fix: Cockpit is open with exposed seat and no canopy; inconsistent with intended enclosed-cockpit jet. Edit a complete clear bubble canopy over seat.

observed objects and assessment: Mongol mounted archer with fur cap, deel, boots, recurved bow, arrow/quiver, saddle and stirrups. Both string segments visible; draw fingers partly hidden.
fault and fix: Airborne stretched gallop and rubble-covered base differ from standing set; horse torso/legs compressed. Repaint calm mounted archer on plain disc.

observed objects and assessment: Thirteenth-century mail, surcoat, great helm, heater shield, upright lance, caparison, stirrups and bridle. Shield hand occluded, no exposed rim grip.
fault and fix: Retain; horse walks rather than stands perfectly still but carries complete coherent kit and reads clearly.

observed objects and assessment: WWI rhomboid tank, riveted hull, side sponson gun, continuous tracks around hull, no turret.
fault and fix: Base has severe mottled high-contrast edge unlike plain cream disc. Edit base only; tank silhouette is right.

observed objects and assessment: Early-Principate helmet/segmentata, gladius at right hip, scutum, caligae without side studs; pilum has a wooden block, thin iron section and pointed tip. Shield hand hidden.
fault and fix: Iron shank still too short and pyramidal tip oversized relative to real pilum proportions; base very veined. Crop-edit longer thin shank/smaller point and calmer base. Previous spear-only and throwing-pose errors are fixed on baseline.

observed objects and assessment: Cold-War low rounded-turret tank, long gun, rear fuel drum, machine gun, continuous tracks and road wheels.
fault and fix: Retain; generic early main-battle-tank subject is appropriate, no modern electronics claim.

observed objects and assessment: Cold-War infantry with steel helmets, AK-pattern rifles, RPG-pattern launcher, boots/web kit and tracked BMP-like vehicle. Grips largely coherent; one soldier kneels.
fault and fix: Huge rose-tan base and multi-figure group shrink subjects at 48 px. Prior audit base-only edit remains useful; vehicle details are generic, not an exact BMP model.

observed objects and assessment: New Kingdom Nubian/Egyptian soldier: feather headband, linen kilt, bare feet, bronze leaf-head spear and arched flat-bottom hide shield. No bow now; correct removal avoids previous unstrung bow.
fault and fix: Left fist hangs beside shield rim with no believable centre support; leather wrist cuff remains despite no bow. Edit bent forearm holding rear central handle, hide hand behind shield, remove cuff. Spear and bare feet are good.

observed objects and assessment: Late-seventeenth-century flintlock with plug bayonet, buff coat, slouch hat, powder charges, hose and closed shoes. Stock supported in both hands.
fault and fix: Forward charging stride differs from standing set; gun identity acceptable for later part of era, not an early matchlock. Repaint upright when lower-priority pose work is reached.

observed objects and assessment: WWII German medium-tank-inspired turret, long gun/muzzle brake, side skirts, cupola and tracks.
fault and fix: Wheel/suspension arrangement is generic and miniature silhouette close to Tank; distinct own Panzer IV painting needed, not tint adjustment.

observed objects and assessment: User-approved v6: fox-fur cap, chiton/chlamys, boots, crescent pelte, one raised and two spare javelins; palm visibly supports raised shaft. Spare shafts run along inner shield side, grip on rear handle visible.
fault and fix: Retain explicit approved exception to standing rule; no renewed claim that its action pose is the set norm. Spare lengths are close but cannot establish exact equality under occlusion.

observed objects and assessment: Three Macedonian-style pikemen with helmets, linen torso armour, small shields and long shafts; visible fingers wrap shafts, boots/sandals and greaves coherent.
fault and fix: Three tiny bodies and chest-centred shields read as a toy squad, not same-height figure; sarissas compressed in length. Repaint one standing phalangite with small left-arm shield and genuinely long sarissa.

observed objects and assessment: Late-medieval/early-Renaissance kettle helmet, plate torso and limb pieces, cloth hose, closed shoes, two hands on pike.
fault and fix: Wide braced stance and shortened pike reduce body scale against standing figures. Repaint upright; no false claim that pike is full historical length.

observed objects and assessment: Swiss mercenary in slashed doublet/hose, feathered beret, breastplate, Katzbalger-like short sword and upright pike; both grips and shoes coherent.
fault and fix: Pike barely taller than soldier, not a long infantry pike. Extend in repaint while managing figure scale. Calendar maps him to Pikeman, so do NOT add a musket based on superseded branch history.

observed objects and assessment: Nineteenth-century kepi, blue wool, ammunition pouch, closed shoes and percussion rifled musket with ramrod/sling; both hands support wood, hammer/lock visible.
fault and fix: Retain; coherent upright ready posture, neutral disc and clear long gun.

observed objects and assessment: Cold-War truck launcher: three axles, elevated tube bank, hydraulic support, cab, connected wheels and rear stabilisers.
fault and fix: Retain; tubes vary slightly in drawn ellipse but no clear structural contradiction at source size.

observed objects and assessment: Simple tunic/cloak, slung petasos-like hat, satchel, staff and sandals; one hand grips staff, other shades eyes naturally.
fault and fix: Large rock under forward foot and leaning pose break plain-disc standing convention. Repaint upright, preserve character and kit.

observed objects and assessment: Woman with layered woven garments, shawl, bedroll/pack, staff and leather sandals; one hand grips staff and other pack strap naturally.
fault and fix: Retain; coherent travelling stance and good adult proportions.

observed objects and assessment: Corinthian-style helmet, linen cuirass, greaves, dory, round aspis with lambda and leather sandals; right spear grip clear, shield arm hidden.
fault and fix: Base has inset second step; simplify to one plain disc. Lambda is intentional historical identity, not accidental text.

observed objects and assessment: Greek-style helmet, bronze cuirass, round decorated shield, dory and greaves; only 256 px source exists.
fault and fix: Hands and shield attachment cannot be authenticated beyond available pixels. No clear defect seen; higher-resolution repaint needed for panel quality, not a fabricated fine-detail pass.

observed objects and assessment: Flying-wing bomber with cockpit, paired intakes, sawtooth trailing edge and curved display stand.
fault and fix: Retain; distinct wing outline and clean connections.

observed objects and assessment: Faceted twin-engine fighter with closed canopy, canted fins, angular wings and twin exhausts on curved stand.
fault and fix: Retain; coherent generic advanced aircraft.

observed objects and assessment: Byzantine skoutatos with conical helmet/mail, lamellar torso, spear, kite shield, boots and short sidearm. Shield grip hidden.
fault and fix: Spear held overhead across face, combat pose rather than standing at rest. Repaint upright eventually. Calendar still names Tagmatic Soldier; do not apply obsolete Varangian-axe direction.

observed objects and assessment: WWII Sherman-inspired cast turret, short gun, bogie suspension, tracks and stowage, no modern reactive armour.
fault and fix: Retain; own WWII painting, no longer the old modern-tank mismatch.

observed objects and assessment: French WWI Adrian helmet, horizon-blue coat, pack, puttees and hobnailed boots; right hand grasps a wooden gun part.
fault and fix: Rifle has bayonet at one end and barrel-like tubes at the other, no coherent butt/receiver; visibly malformed. Repaint standing poilu with complete Lebel-pattern rifle, long needle bayonet, correct stock and action.

observed objects and assessment: Asian elephant with small ears, four limbs, howdah, textile caparison, mahout carrying hooked ankus, rear armed passenger; hands small but plausible.
fault and fix: Small transparent pinhole on left rear leg; tusk tips overly blunt/capped. Repair pinhole on later pass; no weapon mechanism asserted behind howdah wall.

observed objects and assessment: Adult pair, chiton/himation, simple gold hairband/brooches, open wax diptych; visible gesturing, resting and tablet-holding hands plausible. Doric colonnade/Acropolis background.
fault and fix: Retain. Feet outside half-length crop; no inferred footwear.

observed objects and assessment: Mexica pair: feathered eagle headgear, padded textile, macuahuitl, huipil/skirt and jade ornaments; visible hands plausible.
fault and fix: Fan-like headdress/suit is over-elaborate; supporting hand sits uncomfortably near obsidian edge. Repaint toward documented costume and keep hand wholly on handle/wood. Not an anatomical finger-count claim.

observed objects and assessment: AD 1000 elite pair, embroidered robes, mantle, pearl circlet/veil, jewelled closed codex and illuminated open book. Hands coherent.
fault and fix: Hagia Sophia behind them has Ottoman minarets, centuries too late. Edit skyline only to pre-Ottoman basilica.

observed objects and assessment: First-century Briton pair, checked wool mantles, torcs, brooches, tunics, spear and sheathed sword; visible hands coherent, hillfort/cart background plausible.
fault and fix: Retain; no claim that decorative brooch motif is exact excavated type.

observed objects and assessment: New Kingdom elite pair, linen, wigs, broad collars, bracelets, papyrus roll, reed pen and narrow wooden scribal palette with TWO pigment cakes and pen slot. Corrected palette now visibly right.
fault and fix: Background boats have lateen triangular sails instead of period square sails. Edit boats only; keep corrected palette and hands.

observed objects and assessment: 1870s–80s workshop pair: waistcoat, shirt, leather apron; high-neck dress/apron; bound notebook and dividers; flywheel, shafts and furnace. Hands coherent.
fault and fix: Retain; no modern protective-equipment expectation imposed on historical scene.

observed objects and assessment: Mughal c.1600 pair: wrapped turban, jama/sash, bound ledger; veil and embroidered dress/jewellery; inkpot and qalam on desk. Both adults and visible hands coherent.
fault and fix: Retain; broad court setting consistent, no exact named monument claim.

observed objects and assessment: Archived Edo pair: kosode/kimono, obi, pinned hair and topknot; hands naturally folded, timber town/castle background.
fault and fix: Retain archived painting; reviewed despite not one of eleven current factions.

observed objects and assessment: Thirteenth-century representative pair: belted wrap robes, fur caps, boots out of frame, horse tack/reins, sheathed sidearm; visible hand grips reins, woman's hands folded.
fault and fix: Retain; not every woman required aristocratic boqta. No invented claim about hidden footwear.

observed objects and assessment: Late-Republic veteran/surveyor and woman: wool tunic/mantles, fibulae, wax diptych, crossed groma with visible hanging plumb weights and rope; hand grips pole, other holds tablet. Four weights not all visible under hand/rope.
fault and fix: Retain corrected wooden tablets; bronze military diploma is gone. Do not count hidden groma cord as missing.

observed objects and assessment: Fifth-century BCE hoplite/representative woman: raised Corinthian helmet, cuirass, spear/aspis, peplos and cloaks. Visible spear grip natural; shield hand hidden.
fault and fix: Massive fortified city wall/banner backdrop contradicts intended classical Sparta. Edit to unwalled settlement and Taygetus landscape; retain people.

observed objects and assessment: Sixteenth-century merchant pair: slashed sleeves, doublet, coif, brocade dress, ledger, coins/weights and two-pan balance; visible hands natural. Dedicated enlarged crop confirms central suspension, equal-arm brass beam and chains at each end.
fault and fix: Retain. Initial concern about absent beam was disproved by dedicated crop; do not repaint functioning apparatus.
